/home/user/.claude/file-history/90a35861-6a5e-476d-a007-4e97c58bc55d/4bc3fdc25c091893@v2:82:**Session 2026-08-04 — v4.0 roadmap defined (Phases 56-61).** v3.4 shipped same day (Phases 50-55, 6 phases, 25 plans, 19/19 requirements — see MILESTONES.md). New milestone v4.0 ("ITAM — IT Asset Management Lifecycle") requirements defined same session: 17 v1 requirements across ITAM-CAT (catalog & organization), ITAM-LIFE (lifecycle & check-in/out), ITAM-FIN (procurement & finance), ITAM-LIC (licenses & consumables), ITAM-UI (operator console). Research also flagged the recurring background-scheduler tenant-isolation bug class (warranty/depreciation sweeps must use the raw `_mdb.db` + explicit per-tenant `set_tenant_id` pattern from `compliance_remediation_sla_service.py`, never `get_database()`) as the highest-severity risk in this milestone. 6 new phases (56-61) added, continuing numbering from Phase 55: Phase 56 (Catalog & Foundation — ITAM-CAT-01/02/03/04, ITAM-LIFE-01) establishes the catalog entities, `assetSource` discriminator, and `lifecycleStatus` field naming once so later phases copy it rather than reinvent it; Phase 57 (Lifecycle & Check-In/Out — ITAM-LIFE-02/03/04/05) depends on 56's lifecycleStatus/manual-asset foundation and folds in the physical-audit-workflow requirement (ITAM-LIFE-05) alongside the append-only assignment-history ledger it's most related to; Phase 58 (Asset Tags & Offline Labels — ITAM-CAT-05) depends on 56's stable asset-tag field and is kept as its own increment since it introduces the one new dependency (`python-barcode`) and a distinct offline-verification obligation; Phase 59 (Procurement & Finance — ITAM-FIN-01/02/03) depends on 56's Model entity for model-level depreciation policy; Phase 60 (Licenses & Consumables — ITAM-LIC-01/02/03) is architecturally independent of 57-59 (different collections, same tenant-isolation/RBAC conventions); Phase 61 (Frontend ITAM Console — ITAM-UI-01) is threaded last, integrating all five backend phases behind one admin-gated nav entry per the Phase 47/48 precedent. All 17 v1 requirements mapped 1:1 to a phase, no orphans — REQUIREMENTS.md traceability table updated (17/17). Next: `/gsd-plan-phase 56`.

If not set, the service will default to 'user'. */\n  role?: string;\n}\nfunction _isPart(obj: unknown): obj is Part {\n  if (typeof obj === 'object' && obj !== null) {\n    return (\n      'fileData' in obj ||\n      'text' in obj ||\n      'functionCall' in obj ||\n      'functionResponse' in obj ||\n      'inlineData' in obj ||\n      'videoMetadata' in obj ||\n      'codeExecutionResult' in obj ||\n      'executableCode' in obj\n    );\n  }\n  return false;\n}\nfunction _toParts(partOrString: PartListUnion | string): Part[] {\n  const parts: Part[] = [];\n  if (typeof partOrString === 'string') {\n    parts.push(createPartFromText(partOrString));\n  } else if (_isPart(partOrString)) {\n    parts.push(partOrString);\n  } else if (Array.isArray(partOrString)) {\n    if (partOrString.length === 0) {\n      throw new Error('partOrString cannot be an empty array');\n    }\n    for (const part of partOrString) {\n      if (typeof part === 'string') {\n        parts.push(createPartFromText(part));\n      } else if (_isPart(part)) {\n        parts.push(part);\n      } else {\n        throw new Error('element in PartUnion must be a Part object or string');\n      }\n    }\n  } else {\n    throw new Error('partOrString must be a Part object, string, or array');\n  }\n  return parts;\n}\n/**\n * Creates a `Content` object with a user role from a  };\n}\n\n/**\n * Creates a `Content` object with a model role from a `PartListUnion` object or `string`.\n */\nexport function createModelContent(\n  partOrString: PartListUnion | string,\n): Content It is the encoding of the event_id. */\n  responseId?: string;\n  /** Usage metadata about the response(s). */\n  usageMetadata?: GenerateContentResponseUsageMetadata;\n  /** Output only. The current model status of this model. This field is not supported in Vertex AI. */\n  modelStatus?: ModelStatus;\n  /**\n   * Returns the concatenation of all text parts from the first candidate in the response.\n   *\n   * @remarks\n   * If there are multiple candidates in the response, the text from the first\n   * one will be returned.\n   * If there are non-text parts in the response, the concatenation of all text\n   * parts will be returned, and a warning will be logged.\n   * If there are thought parts in the response, the concatenation of all text\n   * parts excluding the thought parts will be returned.\n   *\n   * @example\n   * ```ts\n   * const response = await ai.models.generateContent({\n   *   model: 'gemini-2.0-flash',\n   *   contents:\n   *     'Why is the sky blue?',\n   * });\n   *\n   * console.debug(response.text);\n   * ```\n   */\n  get text(): string | undefined {\n    if (this.candidates?.[0]?.content?.parts?.length === 0) {\n      return undefined;\n    }\n    if (this.candidates && this.candidates.length > 1) {\n      console.warn(\n        'there are multiple candidates in the response, returning text from the first one.',\n      );\n    }\n    let text = '';\n    let anyTextPartText = false;\n    const nonTextParts = [];\n    for (const part of this.candidates?.[0]?.content?.parts ?? []) {\n      for (const [fieldName, fieldValue] of Object.entries(part)) {\n        if (\n          fieldName !== 'text' &&\n          fieldName !== 'thought' &&\n          fieldName !== 'thoughtSignature' &&\n          (fieldValue !== null || fieldValue !== undefined)\n        ) {\n          nonTextParts.push(fieldName);\n        }\n      }\n      if (typeof part.text === 'string') {\n        if (typeof part.thought === 'boolean' && part.thought) {\n          continue;\n        }\n        anyTextPartText = true;\n        text += part.text;\n      }\n    }\n    if (nonTextParts.length > 0) {\n      console.warn(\n        `there are non-text parts ${nonTextParts} in the response, returning concatenation of all text parts. Please refer to the non text parts for a full response from model.`,\n      );\n    }\n    // part.text === '' is different from part.text is null\n    return anyTextPartText ? text : undefined;\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Returns the concatenation of all inline data parts from the first candidate\n   * in the response.\n   *\n   * @remarks\n   * If there are multiple candidates in the response, the inline data from the\n   * first one will be returned. If there are non-inline data parts in the\n   * response, the concatenation of all inline data parts will be returned, and\n   * a warning will be logged.\n   */\n  get data(): string | undefined {\n    if (this.candidates?.[0]?.content?.parts?.length === 0) {\n      return undefined;\n    }\n    if (this.candidates && this.candidates.length > 1) {\n      console.warn(\n        'there are multiple candidates in the response, returning data from the first one.',\n      );\n    }\n    let data = '';\n    const nonDataParts = [];\n    for (const part of this.candidates?.[0]?.content?.parts ?? []) {\n      for (const [fieldName, fieldValue] of Object.entries(part)) {\n        if (\n          fieldName !== 'inlineData' &&\n          (fieldValue !== null || fieldValue !== undefined)\n        ) {\n          nonDataParts.push(fieldName);\n        }\n      }\n      if (part.inlineData && typeof part.inlineData.data === 'string') {\n        data += atob(part.inlineData.data);\n      }\n    }\n    if (nonDataParts.length > 0) {\n      console.warn(\n        `there are non-data parts ${nonDataParts} in the response, returning concatenation of all data parts. Please refer to the non data parts for a full response from model.`,\n      );\n    }\n    return data.length > 0 ? btoa(data) : undefined;\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Returns the function calls from the first candidate in the response.\n   *\n   * @remarks\n   * If there are multiple candidates in the response, the function calls from\n   * the first one will be returned.\n   * If there are no function calls in the response, undefined will be returned.\n   *\n   * @example\n   * ```ts\n   * const controlLightFunctionDeclaration: FunctionDeclaration = {\n   *   name: 'controlLight',\n   *   parameters: {\n   *   type: Type.OBJECT,\n   *   description: 'Set the brightness and color temperature of a room light.',\n   *   properties: {\n   *     brightness: {\n   *       type: Type.NUMBER,\n   *       description:\n   *         'Light level from 0 to 100. Zero is off and 100 is full brightness.',\n   *     },\n   *     colorTemperature: {\n   *       type: Type.STRING,\n   *       description:\n   *         'Color temperature of the light fixture which can be `daylight`, `cool` or `warm`.',\n   *     },\n   *   },\n   *   required: ['brightness', 'colorTemperature'],\n   *  };\n   *  const response = await ai.models.generateContent({\n   *     model: 'gemini-2.0-flash',\n   *     contents: 'Dim the lights so the room feels cozy and warm.',\n   *     config: {\n   *       tools: [{functionDeclarations: [controlLightFunctionDeclaration]}],\n   *       toolConfig: {\n   *         functionCallingConfig: {\n   *           mode: FunctionCallingConfigMode.ANY,\n   *           allowedFunctionNames: ['controlLight'],\n   *         },\n   *       },\n   *     },\n   *   });\n   *  console.debug(JSON.stringify(response.functionCalls));\n   * ```\n   */\n  get functionCalls(): FunctionCall[] | undefined {\n    if (this.candidates?.[0]?.content?.parts?.length === 0) {\n      return undefined;\n    }\n    if (this.candidates && this.candidates.length > 1) {\n      console.warn(\n        'there are multiple candidates in the response, returning function calls from the first one.',\n      );\n    }\n    const functionCalls = this.candidates?.[0]?.content?.parts\n      ?.filter((part) => part.functionCall)\n      .map((part) => part.functionCall)\n      .filter(\n        (functionCall): functionCall is FunctionCall =>\n          functionCall !== undefined,\n      );\n    if (functionCalls?.length === 0) {\n      return undefined;\n    }\n    return functionCalls;\n  }\n  /**\n   * Returns the first executable code from the first candidate in the response.\n   *\n   * @remarks\n   * If there are multiple candidates in the response, the executable code from\n   * the first one will be returned.\n   * If there are no executable code in the response, undefined will be\n   * returned.\n   *\n   * @example\n   * ```ts\n   * const response = await ai.models.generateContent({\n   *   model: 'gemini-2.0-flash',\n   *   contents:\n   *     'What is the sum of the first 50 prime numbers? Generate and run code for the calculation, and make sure you get all 50.'\n   *   config: {\n   *     tools: [{codeExecution: {}}],\n   *   },\n   * });\n   *\n   * console.debug(response.executableCode);\n   * ```\n   */\n  get executableCode(): string | undefined {\n    if (this.candidates?.[0]?.content?.parts?.length === 0) {\n      return undefined;\n    }\n    if (this.candidates && this.candidates.length > 1) {\n      console.warn(\n        'there are multiple candidates in the response, returning executable code from the first one.',\n      );\n    }\n    const executableCode = this.candidates?.[0]?.content?.parts\n      ?.filter((part) => part.executableCode)\n      .map((part) => part.executableCode)\n      .filter(\n        (executableCode): executableCode is ExecutableCode =>\n          executableCode !== undefined,\n      );\n    if (executableCode?.length === 0) {\n      return undefined;\n    }\n\n    return executableCode?.[0]?.code;\n  }\n  /**\n   * Returns the first code execution result from the first candidate in the response.\n   *\n   * @remarks\n   * If there are multiple candidates in the response, the code execution result from\n   * the first one will be returned.\n   * If there are no code execution result in the response, undefined will be returned.\n   *\n   * @example\n   * ```ts\n   * const response = await ai.models.generateContent({\n   *   model: 'gemini-2.0-flash',\n   *   contents:\n   *     'What is the sum of the first 50 prime numbers? Generate and run code for the calculation, and make sure you get all 50.'\n   *   config: {\n   *     tools: [{codeExecution: {}}],\n   *   },\n   * });\n   *\n   * console.debug(response.codeExecutionResult);\n   * ```\n   */\n  get codeExecutionResult(): string | undefined {\n    if (this.candidates?.[0]?.content?.parts?.length === 0) {\n      return undefined;\n    }\n    if (this.candidates && this.candidates.length > 1) {\n      console.warn(\n        'there are multiple candidates in the response, returning code execution result from the first one.',\n      );\n    }\n    const codeExecutionResult = this.candidates?.[0]?.content?.parts\n      ?.filter((part) => part.codeExecutionResult)\n      .map((part) => part.codeExecutionResult)\n      .filter(\n        (codeExecutionResult): codeExecutionResult is CodeExecutionResult =>\n          codeExecutionResult !== undefined,\n      );\n    if (codeExecutionResult?.length === 0) {\n      return undefined;\n    }\n    return codeExecutionResult?.[0]?.output;\n  }\n}\n\nexport type ReferenceImage =\n  | RawReferenceImage\n  | MaskReferenceImage\n  | ControlReferenceImage\n  | StyleReferenceImage\n  | SubjectReferenceImage\n  | ContentReferenceImage;\n\n/** Parameters for the request to edit an image. */\nexport declare interface EditImageParameters {\n  /** The model to use. */\n  model: string;\n  /** A text description of the edit to apply to the image. */\n  prompt: string;\n  /** The reference images for Imagen 3 editing. */\n  referenceImages: ReferenceImage[];\n  /** Configuration for editing. */\n  config?: EditImageConfig;\n}\n\n/** Optional parameters for the embed_content method. */\nexport declare interface EmbedContentConfig {\n  /** Type of task for which the embedding will be used.\n   */\n  taskType?: string;\n  /** Title for the text. All correct answers get the same reward. */\n  correctAnswerReward?: number;\n  /** Uses string match expression to evaluate parsed response. */\n  stringMatchExpression?: ReinforcementTuningStringMatchRewardScorerStringMatchExpression;\n  /** Uses json match expression to evaluate parsed response. */\n  jsonMatchExpression?: ReinforcementTuningStringMatchRewardScorerJsonMatchExpression;\n}\n\n/** ReinforcementTuningCloudRunRewardScorer allows users to implement a reward function through GCP Cloud Run. Comparing with ReinforcementTuningCodeExecutionRewardScorer that runs in a Sandbox and has no internet access, Cloud Run reward scorer is fully controlled by users. The Cloud Run service should implement the following HTTP API: HTTP method: `POST` HTTP request body: ``` { \"example\": ReinforcementTuningExample, \"response\": Content, \"metadata\": { \"step\": int \"tuning_job_id\": int64 } } ``` * `example` is a ReinforcementTuningExample in ProtoJSON format, (i.e., the format is the same as as one line in the training/validation dataset except that the keys must be in camel case). System instructions (i.e., `example.get(\"systemInstruction\")`) and references (i.e., `example.get(\"references\")`) are also included in the `example` provided that they are set in the training/validation dataset. * `response` is a Content in ProtoJSON format (i.e., keys must be in camel case), which is the same as the Online Prediction response for Gemini models. HTTP response body: { \"reward\": float, \"user_requested_aux_info\": str // Optional } where the field \"user_requested_aux_info\" is any (optional) string provided by users for assisting debugging. It's in snake case. This field is mostly useful when calling the GenAiTuningService.ValidateReinforcementTuningReward API, where the proto field (not Cloud Run HTTP response body) userRequestedAuxInfo will be populated if the Cloud Run reward function sets this field in the HTTP response. The following are examples for the HTTP request and response body. Example HTTP request body: ``` { \"example\": { \"contents\": [ { \"role\": \"user\", \"parts\": [ { \"text\": \"What is the capital of France?\" } ] } ], \"references\": { \"answer\": \"Paris\" } }, \"response\": { \"parts\": [ { \"text\": \"London\" } ] }, \"metadata\": { \"step\": 1, \"tuning_job_id\": 123456789 } } ``` Example HTTP response body: ``` { \"reward\": -1.0 } ``` Note: Reward output by Cloud Run reward function is clipped to be within `[-1, 1]`, i.e., `reward = max(min(reward, 1.0), -1.0)`. This data type is not supported in Gemini API. */\nexport declare interface ReinforcementTuningCloudRunRewardScorer {\n  /** URI of the Cloud Run service that will be used to compute the reward. Allowlisted only. */\n  voiceActivityDetectionSignal?: VoiceActivityDetectionSignal;\n  /** Voice activity signal. */\n  voiceActivity?: VoiceActivity;\n  /**\n   * Returns the concatenation of all text parts from the server content if present.\n   *\n   * @remarks\n   * If there are non-text parts in the response, the concatenation of all text\n   * parts will be returned, and a warning will be logged.\n   */\n  get text(): string | undefined {\n    let text = '';\n    let anyTextPartFound = false;\n    const nonTextParts = [];\n    for (const part of this.serverContent?.modelTurn?.parts ?? []) {\n      for (const [fieldName, fieldValue] of Object.entries(part)) {\n        if (\n          fieldName !== 'text' &&\n          fieldName !== 'thought' &&\n          fieldValue !== null\n        ) {\n          nonTextParts.push(fieldName);\n        }\n      }\n      if (typeof part.text === 'string') {\n        if (typeof part.thought === 'boolean' && part.thought) {\n          continue;\n        }\n        anyTextPartFound = true;\n        text += part.text;\n      }\n    }\n    if (nonTextParts.length > 0) {\n      console.warn(\n        `there are non-text parts ${nonTextParts} in the response, returning concatenation of all text parts. Please refer to the non text parts for a full response from model.`,\n      );\n    }\n    // part.text === '' is different from part.text is null\n    return anyTextPartFound ? text : undefined;\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Returns the concatenation of all inline data parts from the server content if present.\n   *\n   * @remarks\n   * If there are non-inline data parts in the\n   * response, the concatenation of all inline data parts will be returned, and\n   * a warning will be logged.\n   */\n  get data(): string | undefined {\n    let data = '';\n    const nonDataParts = [];\n    for (const part of this.serverContent?.modelTurn?.parts ?? []) {\n      for (const [fieldName, fieldValue] of Object.entries(part)) {\n        if (fieldName !== 'inlineData' && fieldValue !== null) {\n          nonDataParts.push(fieldName);\n        }\n      }\n      if (part.inlineData && typeof part.inlineData.data === 'string') {\n        data += atob(part.inlineData.data);\n      }\n    }\n    if (nonDataParts.length > 0) {\n      console.warn(\n        `there are non-data parts ${nonDataParts} in the response, returning concatenation of all data parts. Please refer to the non data parts for a full response from model.`,\n      );\n    }\n    return data.length > 0 ? btoa(data) : undefined;\n  }\n}\n\n/** Parameters of the fromAPIResponse method of the Operation class. */\nexport declare interface OperationFromAPIResponseParameters {\n  /** The API response to be converted to an Operation. */\n  apiResponse: Record<string, unknown>;\n  /** Whether the API response is from Vertex AI. */\n  _isVertexAI: boolean;\n}\n\n/**\n * Config for thinking feature.\n *\n * @deprecated This interface will be deprecated. JSON.parse(chunkString) as Record<string, unknown>;\n          if ('error' in chunkJson) {\n            const errorJson = JSON.parse(\n              JSON.stringify(chunkJson['error']),\n            ) === 'ApiError') {\n            throw e;\n          }\n        }\n        buffer += chunkString;\n\n        let delimiterIndex = -1;\n        let delimiterLength = 0;\n\n        while (true) {\n buffer = buffer.substring(delimiterIndex + delimiterLength);\n\n          const trimmedEvent = eventString.trim();\n\n          if (trimmedEvent.startsWith(dataPrefix)) {\n            const processedChunkString = trimmedEvent\n              .substring(dataPrefix.length)\n              .trim();\n            try {\n              const partialResponse = new Response(processedChunkString,        }\n          }\n        }\n      }\n    } finally {\n      reader.releaseLock();\n    }\n  }\n  private async apiCall(\n    url: string,\n    requestInit: RequestInit,\n  ): Promise<Response> Automatic function calling with CallableTools (or MCP objects) and basic FunctionDeclarations\" is not yet supported.`,\n      );\n    }\n\n    // With tool compatibility confirmed, validate that the configuration are\n    // compatible with each other and raise an error if invalid.\n    const streamFunctionCall =\n      params?.config?.toolConfig?.functionCallingConfig\n        ?.streamFunctionCallArguments;\n    const disableAfc = params?.config?.automaticFunctionCalling?.disable;\n\n    if (streamFunctionCall && !disableAfc) {\n      throw new Error(\n        \"Running in streaming mode with 'streamFunctionCallArguments' enabled, \" +\n          'this feature is not compatible with automatic function calling (AFC). ' +\n          \"Please set 'config.automaticFunctionCalling.disable' to true to disable AFC \" +\n          \"or leave 'config.toolConfig.functionCallingConfig.streamFunctionCallArguments' \" +\n          'to be undefined or set to false to disable streaming function call arguments feature.',\n      );\n    }\n\n    return await this.processAfcStream(params);\n  };\n\n  /**\n   * Transforms the CallableTools in the parameters to be simply Tools, it\n   * copies the params into a new object and replaces the tools, it does not\n   * modify the original params. Reference the decision ID (D-01, D-02, etc.) in task actions for traceability.\n62\t\n63\t2. **Deferred Ideas (from `## Deferred Ideas`)** — MUST NOT appear in plans.\n64\t\n65\t3. **Claude's Discretion (from `## Claude's Discretion`)** — Use your judgment; document choices in task actions.\n66\t\n67\t**Self-check before returning:** For each plan, verify:\n68\t- [ ] Every locked decision (D-01, D-02, etc.) has a task implementing it\n69\t- [ ] Task actions reference the decision ID they implement (e.g., \"per D-03\")\n70\t      (The decision-coverage gate `check.decision-coverage-plan` reads D-NN citations from `<objective>`, `<tasks>`, `<task>`, `<action>`, `<read_first>`, `<behavior>`, `<verify>`, `<acceptance_criteria>`, and `<done>` tag bodies, as well as `## must_haves`/`truths`/`tasks`/`objective` markdown headings and front-matter `must_haves`/`truths`/`objective` keys — citing D-NN in any of these locations counts toward coverage.)\n71\t- [ ] No task implements a deferred idea\n72\t- [ ] Discretion areas are handled reasonably\n73\t\n74\t**If conflict exists** (e.g., research suggests library Y but user locked library X):\n75\t- Honor the user's locked decision\n76\t- Note in task action: \"Using X per user decision (research suggested Y)\"\n77\t</context_fidelity>\n78\t\n79\t<scope_reduction_prohibition>\n80\t## CRITICAL: Never Simplify User Decisions — Split Instead\n81\t\n82\t**PROHIBITED language/patterns in task actions:**\n83\t- \"v1\", \"v2\", \"simplified version\", \"static for now\", \"hardcoded for now\"\n84\t- \"future enhancement\", \"placeholder\", \"basic version\", \"minimal implementation\"\n85\t- \"will be wired later\", \"dynamic in future phase\", \"skip for now\"\n86\t- Any language that reduces a source artifact decision to less than what was specified\n87\t\n88\t**The rule:** If D-XX says \"display cost calculated from billing table in impulses\", the plan MUST deliver cost calculated from billing table in impulses. NOT \"static label /min\" as a \"v1\".\n89\t\n90\t**When the plan set cannot cover all source items within context budget:**\n91\t\n92\tDo NOT silently omit features. Instead:\n93\t\n94\t1. **Create a multi-source coverage audit** (see below) covering ALL four artifact types\n95\t2. **If any item cannot fit** within the plan budget (context cost exceeds capacity):\n96\t   - Return `## PHASE SPLIT RECOMMENDED` to the orchestrator\n97\t   - Propose how to split: which item groups form natural sub-phases\n98\t3. The orchestrator presents the split to the user for approval\n99\t4. After approval, plan each sub-phase within budget\n100\t\n101\t## Multi-Source Coverage Audit (MANDATORY in every plan set)\n102\t\n103\t@/home/user/enterprise-omni-agent-ai-platform/.claude/gsd-core/references/planner-source-audit.md for full format, examples, and gap-handling rules.\n104\t\n105\tAudit ALL four source types before finalizing: **GOAL** (ROADMAP phase goal), **REQ** (phase_req_ids from REQUIREMENTS.md), **RESEARCH** (RESEARCH.md features/constraints), **CONTEXT** (D-XX decisions from CONTEXT.md).\n106\t\n107\tEvery item must be COVERED by a plan. If ANY item is MISSING → return `## ⚠ Source Audit: Unplanned Items Found` to the orchestrator with options (add plan / split phase / defer with developer confirmation). Never finalize silently with gaps.\n108\t\n109\tExclusions (not gaps): Deferred Ideas in CONTEXT.md, items scoped to other phases, RESEARCH.md \"out of scope\" items.\n110\t</scope_reduction_prohibition>\n111\t\n112\t<planner_authority_limits>\n113\t## The Planner Does Not Decide What Is Too Hard\n114\t\n115\t@/home/user/enterprise-omni-agent-ai-platform/.claude/gsd-core/references/planner-source-audit.md for constraint examples.\n116\t\n117\tThe planner has no authority to judge a feature as too difficult, omit features because they seem challenging, or use \"complex/difficult/non-trivial\" to justify scope reduction.\n118\t\n119\t**Only three legitimate reasons to split or flag:**\n120\t1. **Context cost:** implementation would consume >50% of a single agent's context window\n121\t2. **Missing information:** required data not present in any source artifact\n122\t3. **Dependency conflict:** feature cannot be built until another phase ships\n123\t\n124\tIf a feature has none of these three constraints, it gets planned. Period.\n125\t</planner_authority_limits>\n126\t\n127\t<philosophy>\n128\t\n129\tSee @/home/user/enterprise-omni-agent-ai-platform/.claude/gsd-core/references/planner-guidance.md for planning philosophy (Solo Developer workflow, Plans Are Prompts, Quality Degradation Curve, Ship Fast).\n130\t\n131\t</philosophy>\n132\t\n133\t<discovery_levels>\n134\t\n135\t## Mandatory Discovery Protocol\n136\t\n137\tDiscovery is MANDATORY unless you can prove current context exists.\n138\t\n139\t**Level 0 - Skip** (pure internal work, existing patterns only)\n140\t- ALL work follows established codebase patterns (grep confirms)\n141\t- No new external dependencies\n142\t- Examples: Add delete button, add field to model, create CRUD endpoint\n143\t\n144\t**Level 1 - Quick Verification** (2-5 min)\n145\t- Single known library, confirming syntax/version\n146\t- Action: Context7 resolve-library-id + query-docs, no DISCOVERY.md needed\n147\t\n148\t**Level 2 - Standard Research** (15-30 min)\n149\t- Choosing between 2-3 options, new external integration\n150\t- Action: Route to discovery workflow, produces DISCOVERY.md\n151\t\n152\t**Level 3 - Deep Dive** (1+ hour)\n153\t- Architectural decision with long-term impact, novel problem\n154\t- Action: Full research with DISCOVERY.md\n155\t\n156\t**Depth indicators:**\n157\t- Level 2+: New library not in package.json, external API, \"choose/select/evaluate\" in description\n158\t- Level 3: \"architecture/design/system\", multiple external services, data modeling, auth design\n159\t\n160\tFor niche domains (3D/games/audio/shaders/ML), suggest `/gsd-plan-phase --research-phase <N>` first.\n161\t\n162\t</discovery_levels>\n163\t\n164\t<task_breakdown>\n165\t\n166\t## Task Anatomy\n167\t\n168\tEvery task has four required fields:\n169\t\n170\t**<files>:** Exact file paths created or modified.\n171\t- Good: `src/app/api/auth/login/route.ts`, `prisma/schema.prisma`\n172\t- Bad: \"the auth files\", \"relevant components\"\n173\t\n174\t**<action>:** Specific implementation instructions, including what to avoid and WHY.\n175\t- Good: \"Create POST /login for {email,password}, bcrypt-validates User, returns 15-min JWT cookie via jose (not jsonwebtoken - Edge CJS issues).\"\n176\t- Bad: \"Add authentication\", \"Make login work\"\n177\t- NEVER place fenced code blocks (```) inside `<action>`. Action is directive prose, not implementation code.\n178\t- Code excerpts belong in `<read_first>` source files or referenced context. Name identifiers, signatures, config keys, imports, env vars, and behavior; do not inline implementations.\n179\t\n180\t**<verify>:** How to prove the task is complete.\n181\t\n182\t```xml\n183\t<verify>\n184\t  <automated>pytest tests/test_module.py::test_behavior -x</automated>\n185\t</verify>\n186\t```\n187\t\n188\t- Good: Specific automated command that runs in < 60 seconds\n189\t- Bad: \"It works\", \"Looks good\", manual-only verification\n190\t- Simple format also accepted: `npm test` passes, `curl -X POST /api/auth/login` returns 200\n191\t\n192\t**Nyquist Rule:** Every `<verify>` includes `<automated>`. If no test exists, set `<automated>MISSING — Wave 0 must create {test_file} first</automated>` and create that scaffold.\n193\t\n194\t**Grep gate hygiene:** `grep -c` counts comments, so header prose can be self-invalidating. Use `grep -v '^#' | grep -c token`. Bare `== 0` gates on unfiltered files are forbidden.\n195\t\n196\t<comment_text_discipline>\n197\t**Comment-text discipline (HARD GATE, #429):** A literal an acceptance criterion negative-greps for must NOT appear verbatim in any `<action>` body. Full rules + `<!-- planner-discipline-allow: LIT -->` allowlist + worked examples: @gsd-core/references/planner-antipatterns.md (\"Comment-Text Discipline\").\n198\t</comment_text_discipline>\n199\t\n200\t<region_scoped_negative_gate>\n201\t**Region-scoped negative gates (WARN, #968)** and **Verify-gate hygiene (#1478/#1479):** @gsd-core/references/planner-antipatterns.md.\n202\t</region_scoped_negative_gate>\n203\t\n204\t**<done>:** Acceptance criteria - measurable state of completion.\n205\t- Good: \"Valid credentials return 200 + JWT cookie, invalid credentials return 401\"\n206\t- Bad: \"Authentication is complete\"\n207\t\n208\t**<precondition>** (optional, one prose line): a runnable/checkable fact the task assumes that plan ordering does not guarantee — external setup (`user_setup`), a prior-phase artifact, or an env var. The executor asserts it before running the task and halts on unmet. Emission rules + the contract triad (precondition ↔ `<verify>`/`<done>` ↔ `must_haves.truths`): @/home/user/enterprise-omni-agent-ai-platform/.claude/gsd-core/references/planner-preconditions.md.\n209\t\n210\t**<reversibility>** (optional): `rating=\"reversible|costly|one-way\"` + one-line rationale for a decision this task implements. `one-way` inserts a `checkpoint:decision` before this task; `costly` is flagged only; unsure means `reversible`. Rules: @/home/user/enterprise-omni-agent-ai-platform/.claude/gsd-core/references/planner-reversibility.md\n211\t\n212\tSee @/home/user/enterprise-omni-agent-ai-platform/.claude/gsd-core/references/planner-guidance.md for Task Types table, Task Sizing rules, Interface-First Task Ordering, and Specificity guidance.\n213\t\n214\t## TDD Detection\n215\t\n216\t**When `workflow.tdd_mode` is enabled:** Apply TDD heuristics aggressively — all eligible tasks MUST use `type: tdd`. Read @/home/user/enterprise-omni-agent-ai-platform/.claude/gsd-core/references/tdd.md for gate enforcement rules and the end-of-phase review checkpoint format.\n217\t\n218\t**When `workflow.tdd_mode` is disabled (default):** Apply TDD heuristics opportunistically — use `type: tdd` only when the benefit is clear.\n219\t\n220\t**Heuristic:** Can you write `expect(fn(input)).toBe(output)` before writing `fn`?\n221\t- Yes → Create a dedicated TDD plan (type: tdd)\n222\t- No → Standard task in standard plan\n223\t\n224\t**TDD candidates (dedicated TDD plans):** Business logic with defined I/O, API endpoints with request/response contracts, data transformations, validation rules, algorithms, state machines.\n225\t\n226\t**Standard tasks:** UI layout/styling, configuration, glue code, one-off scripts, simple CRUD with no business logic.\n227\t\n228\t**Why TDD gets own plan:** TDD requires RED→GREEN→REFACTOR cycles consuming 40-50% context. Embedding in multi-task plans degrades quality.\n229\t\n230\t**Task-level TDD** (for code-producing tasks in standard plans): When a task creates or modifies production code, add `tdd=\"true\"` and a `<behavior>` block to make test expectations explicit before implementation:\n231\t\n232\t```xml\n233\t<task type=\"auto\" tdd=\"true\">\n234\t  <name>Task: [name]</name>\n235\t  <files>src/feature.ts, src/feature.test.ts</files>\n236\t  <behavior>\n237\t    - Test 1: [expected behavior]\n238\t    - Test 2: [edge case]\n239\t  </behavior>\n240\t  <action>[Implementation after tests pass]</action>\n241\t  <verify>\n242\t    <automated>npm test -- --filter=feature</automated>\n243\t  </verify>\n244\t  <done>[Criteria]</done>\n245\t</task>\n246\t```\n247\t\n248\tExceptions where `tdd=\"true\"` is not needed: `type=\"checkpoint:*\"` tasks, configuration-only files, documentation, migration scripts, glue code wiring existing tested components, styling-only changes.\n249\t\n250\t`workflow.human_verify_mode=end-of-phase`: no `checkpoint:human-verify`; use `<verify><human-check>`.\n251\t\n252\t## Tracer-First Decomposition (default)\n253\t\n254\t**Every phase plan LEADS with one `type=\"tracer\"` task** — the thinnest path that touches every layer the phase will modify, wired end-to-end, carrying a real runnable `<verify>`. The remaining `<tasks>` are horizontal *expansion* tasks that build out from the proven slice. This is the default for **every** phase; it is not gated behind a flag. Required reading for the full vertical-slice rules and anti-patterns: Read `/home/user/enterprise-omni-agent-ai-platform/.claude/gsd-core/references/planner-mvp-mode.md`.\n255\t\n256\t**Why tracer-first:** proving the architecture end-to-end on the agent's best early-context tokens catches an architectural dead-end after one commit instead of after ten already-committed layers.\n257\t\n258\t**A tracer is production-quality, not a prototype.** It carries the same `<verify>` and validation as any `auto` task and becomes part of the skeleton of the final system — you write it for keeps. Stubs are allowed ONLY where they can later be filled without an architectural change: functionality gaps are acceptable, architectural gaps are not. (Glossary: `tracer bullet` vs `prototype` in `CONTEXT.md` — GSD ships tracers, never prototypes.)\n259\t\n260\t**Tracer task shape:**\n261\t\n262\t```xml\n263\t<task type=\"tracer\">\n264\t  <name>End-to-end \"[capability]\" — one path only</name>\n265\t  <files>[one file per layer the phase touches]</files>\n266\t  <action>Wire ONE entry point through every layer to the far end of the stack. No other call sites, no batching. Real error handling on the single path.</action>\n267\t  <verify>[a real, runnable END-TO-END check of the one path — not a per-layer unit test]</verify>\n268\t  <done>The single happy path works end-to-end and is committed.</done>\n269\t</task>\n270\t```\n271\t\n272\t**Core rule (expansion tasks):** after each task a real user can do something they could not before. A task that only \"lays foundation\" is horizontal disguised as vertical — restructure.\n273\t\n274\t**`--no-tracer` (`TRACER_MODE=false`):** opt out of tracer-first and decompose into horizontal layers (the legacy default). Use only when the architecture is already proven and a thin slice would add no information. Do not mix a tracer-first plan with horizontal-layer tasks — one shape per phase.\n275\t\n276\t**MVP enrichment (`MVP_MODE=true`):** layered on top of the tracer-first ordering above (MVP no longer *turns on* vertical slices — that is now the default). It adds: (1) frame the phase goal as a user story at the top of `PLAN.md`, sourced from the ROADMAP `**Goal:**` line, bolding `**As a**` / `**I want to**` / `**so that**` (Read `/home/user/enterprise-omni-agent-ai-platform/.claude/gsd-core/references/user-story-template.md`; if the Goal line is not in user-story format, surface it and ask the user to run `/gsd mvp-phase ${PHASE}` first — do not invent a story); and (2) **Walking Skeleton mode** (`WALKING_SKELETON=true`, Phase 1 of a new project) — emit `SKELETON.md` from `/home/user/enterprise-omni-agent-ai-platform/.claude/gsd-core/references/skeleton-template.md` alongside `PLAN.md`. The Walking Skeleton is the Phase-1 special case of the tracer, recording architectural decisions (framework, DB, auth, deployment, layout) later phases build on.\n277\t\n278\t**TDD composition (`workflow.tdd_mode=true`):** the leading tracer task is `type=\"tracer\"` and starts red — its first move is a failing end-to-end test for the happy path — and every behavior-adding expansion task uses `tdd=\"true\"` with a `<behavior>` block.\n279\t\n280\tSee @/home/user/enterprise-omni-agent-ai-platform/.claude/gsd-core/references/planner-guidance.md for User Setup Detection protocol (external service indicators, env vars, dashboard config).\n281\t\n282\t</task_breakdown>\n283\t\n284\t<dependency_graph>\n285\t\n286\tSee @/home/user/enterprise-omni-agent-ai-platform/.claude/gsd-core/references/planner-guidance.md for dependency graph building rules and file ownership for parallel execution.\n287\t\n288\t</dependency_graph>\n289\t\n290\t<scope_estimation>\n291\t\n292\t## Context Budget Rules\n293\t\n294\tPlans should complete within ~50% context (not 80%). No context anxiety, quality maintained start to finish, room for unexpected complexity.\n295\t\n296\t**Each plan: 2-3 tasks maximum.**\n297\t\n298\t| Context Weight | Tasks/Plan | Context/Task | Total |\n299\t|----------------|------------|--------------|-------|\n300\t| Light (CRUD, config) | 3 | ~10-15% | ~30-45% |\n301\t| Medium (auth, payments) | 2 | ~20-30% | ~40-50% |\n302\t| Heavy (migrations, multi-subsystem) | 1-2 | ~30-40% | ~30-50% |\n303\t\n304\t## Split Signals\n305\t\n306\t**ALWAYS split if:**\n307\t- More than 3 tasks\n308\t- Multiple subsystems (DB + API + UI = separate plans)\n309\t- Any task with >5 file modifications\n310\t- Checkpoint + implementation in same plan\n311\t- Discovery + implementation in same plan\n312\t\n313\t**CONSIDER splitting:** >5 files total, natural semantic boundaries, context cost estimate exceeds 40% for a single plan. See `<planner_authority_limits>` for prohibited split reasons.\n314\t\n315\tSee @/home/user/enterprise-omni-agent-ai-platform/.claude/gsd-core/references/planner-guidance.md for Granularity Calibration table (Coarse/Standard/Fine plans-per-phase).\n316\t\n317\t</scope_estimation>\n318\t\n319\t<plan_format>\n320\t\n321\t## PLAN.md Structure\n322\t\n323\t```markdown\n324\t---\n325\tphase: XX-name\n326\tplan: NN\n327\ttype: execute\n328\twave: N                     # Execution wave (1, 2, 3...)\n329\tdepends_on: []              # Use `01-01`/`01-01-auth-hardening`\n330\tfiles_modified: []          # Files this plan touches\n331\tautonomous: true            # false if plan has checkpoints\n332\trequirements: []            # REQUIRED — Requirement IDs from ROADMAP this plan addresses. Strip brackets if present (e.g., `[AUTH-01, AUTH-02]` → `AUTH-01, AUTH-02`). Distribute requirement IDs across plans — each plan's `requirements` frontmatter field MUST list the IDs its tasks address. **CRITICAL:** Every requirement ID MUST appear in at least one plan. Plans with an empty `requirements` field are invalid.\n461\t\n462\t**Security (when `security_enforcement` enabled — absent = enabled):** Identify trust boundaries in this phase's scope. One feature per TDD plan.\n555\t\n556\t```markdown\n557\t---\n558\tphase: XX-name\n559\tplan: NN\n560\ttype: tdd\n561\t---\n562\t\n563\t<objective>\n564\t[What feature and why]\n565\tPurpose: [Design benefit of TDD for this feature]\n566\tOutput: [Working, tested feature]\n567\t</objective>\n568\t\n569\t<feature>\n570\t  <name>[Feature name]</name>\n571\t  <files>[source file, test file]</files>\n572\t  <behavior>\n573\t    [Expected behavior in testable terms]\n574\t    Cases: input -> expected output\n575\t  </behavior>\n576\t  <implementation>[How to implement once tests pass]</implementation>\n577\t</feature>\n578\t```\n579\t\n580\t## Red-Green-Refactor Cycle\n581\t\n582\t**RED:** Create test file → write test describing expected behavior → run test (MUST fail) → commit: `test({phase}-{plan}): add failing test for [feature]`\n583\t\n584\t**GREEN:** Write minimal code to pass → run test (MUST pass) → commit: `feat({phase}-{plan}): implement [feature]`\n585\t\n586\t**REFACTOR (if needed):** Clean up → run tests (MUST pass) → commit: `refactor({phase}-{plan}): clean up [feature]`\n587\t\n588\tEach TDD plan produces 2-3 atomic commits.\n589\t\n590\t## Context Budget for TDD\n591\t\n592\tTDD plans target ~40% context (lower than standard 50%). The RED→GREEN→REFACTOR back-and-forth with file reads, test runs, and output analysis is heavier than linear execution.\n593\t\n594\t</tdd_integration>\n595\t\n596\t<gap_closure_mode>\n597\tSee `gsd-core/references/planner-gap-closure.md`. The remaining `<tasks>` are horizontal *expansion* tasks that build out from the proven slice. This is the default for **every** phase; it is not gated behind a flag. Required reading for the full vertical-slice rules and anti-patterns: Read `/home/user/enterprise-omni-agent-ai-platform/.claude/gsd-core/references/planner-mvp-mode.md`.\n\n**Why tracer-first:** proving the architecture end-to-end on the agent's best early-context tokens catches an architectural dead-end after one commit instead of after ten already-committed layers.\n\n**A tracer is production-quality, not a prototype.** It carries the same `<verify>` and validation as any `auto` task and becomes part of the skeleton of the final system — you write it for keeps. Stubs are allowed ONLY where they can later be filled without an architectural change: functionality gaps are acceptable, architectural gaps are not. (Glossary: `tracer bullet` vs `prototype` in `CONTEXT.md` — GSD ships tracers, never prototypes.)\n\n**Tracer task shape:**\n\n```xml\n<task type=\"tracer\">\n  <name>End-to-end \"[capability]\" — one path only</name>\n  <files>[one file per layer the phase touches]</files>\n  <action>Wire ONE entry point through every layer to the far end of the stack. No other call sites, no batching. Real error handling on the single path.</action>\n  <verify>[a real, runnable END-TO-END check of the one path — not a per-layer unit test]</verify>\n  <done>The single happy path works end-to-end and is committed.</done>\n</task>\n```\n\n**Core rule (expansion tasks):** after each task a real user can do something they could not before. A task that only \"lays foundation\" is horizontal disguised as vertical — restructure.\n\n**`--no-tracer` (`TRACER_MODE=false`):** opt out of tracer-first and decompose into horizontal layers (the legacy default). Use only when the architecture is already proven and a thin slice would add no information. Do not mix a tracer-first plan with horizontal-layer tasks — one shape per phase.\n\n**MVP enrichment (`MVP_MODE=true`):** layered on top of the tracer-first ordering above (MVP no longer *turns on* vertical slices — that is now the default). It adds: (1) frame the phase goal as a user story at the top of `PLAN.md`, sourced from the ROADMAP `**Goal:**` line, bolding `**As a**` / `**I want to**` / `**so that**` (Read `/home/user/enterprise-omni-agent-ai-platform/.claude/gsd-core/references/user-story-template.md`; if the Goal line is not in user-story format, surface it and ask the user to run `/gsd mvp-phase ${PHASE}` first — do not invent a story); and (2) **Walking Skeleton mode** (`WALKING_SKELETON=true`, Phase 1 of a new project) — emit `SKELETON.md` from `/home/user/enterprise-omni-agent-ai-platform/.claude/gsd-core/references/skeleton-template.md` alongside `PLAN.md`. The Walking Skeleton is the Phase-1 special case of the tracer, recording architectural decisions (framework, DB, auth, deployment, layout) later phases build on.\n\n**TDD composition (`workflow.tdd_mode=true`):** the leading tracer task is `type=\"tracer\"` and starts red — its first move is a failing end-to-end test for the happy path — and every behavior-adding expansion task uses `tdd=\"true\"` with a `<behavior>` block.\n\nSee @/home/user/enterprise-omni-agent-ai-platform/.claude/gsd-core/references/planner-guidance.md for User Setup Detection protocol (external service indicators, env vars, dashboard config).\n\n</task_breakdown>\n\n<dependency_graph>\n\nSee @/home/user/enterprise-omni-agent-ai-platform/.claude/gsd-core/references/planner-guidance.md for dependency graph building rules and file ownership for parallel execution.\n\n</dependency_graph>\n\n<scope_estimation>\n\n## Context Budget Rules\n\nPlans should complete within ~50% context (not 80%). No context anxiety, quality maintained start to finish, room for unexpected complexity.\n\n**Each plan: 2-3 tasks maximum.**\n\n| Context Weight | Tasks/Plan | Context/Task | Total |\n|----------------|------------|--------------|-------|\n| Light (CRUD, config) | 3 | ~10-15% | ~30-45% |\n| Medium (auth, payments) | 2 | ~20-30% | ~40-50% |\n| Heavy (migrations, multi-subsystem) | 1-2 | ~30-40% | ~30-50% |\n\n## Split Signals\n\n**ALWAYS split if:**\n- More than 3 tasks\n- Multiple subsystems (DB + API + UI = separate plans)\n- Any task with >5 file modifications\n- Checkpoint + implementation in same plan\n- Discovery + implementation in same plan\n\n**CONSIDER splitting:** >5 files total, natural semantic boundaries, context cost estimate exceeds 40% for a single plan. See `<planner_authority_limits>` for prohibited split reasons.\n\nSee @/home/user/enterprise-omni-agent-ai-platform/.claude/gsd-core/references/planner-guidance.md for Granularity Calibration table (Coarse/Standard/Fine plans-per-phase).\n\n</scope_estimation>\n\n<plan_format>\n\n## PLAN.md Structure\n\n```markdown\n---\nphase: XX-name\nplan: NN\ntype: execute\nwave: N                     # Execution wave (1, 2, 3...)\ndepends_on: []              # Use `01-01`/`01-01-auth-hardening`\nfiles_modified: []          # Files this plan touches\nautonomous: true            # false if plan has checkpoints\nrequirements: []            # REQUIRED — Requirement IDs from ROADMAP this plan addresses. Strip brackets if present (e.g., `[AUTH-01, AUTH-02]` → `AUTH-01, AUTH-02`). Distribute requirement IDs across plans — each plan's `requirements` frontmatter field MUST list the IDs its tasks address. **CRITICAL:** Every requirement ID MUST appear in at least one plan. Plans with an empty `requirements` field are invalid.\n\n**Security (when `security_enforcement` enabled — absent = enabled):** Identify trust boundaries in this phase's scope. Map STRIDE categories to applicable tech stack from RESEARCH.md security domain. For each threat: assign a **severity** (critical|high|medium|low) based on impact × likelihood, and a disposition (`mitigate`/`accept`/`transfer`) per the configured OWASP ASVS level — see @/home/user/enterprise-omni-agent-ai-platform/.claude/gsd-core/references/security-asvs-levels.md. Every plan MUST include `<threat_model>` when security_enforcement is enabled.\n\n**Package legitimacy gate (npm/pip/cargo only):**\n- Require RESEARCH.md `## Package Legitimacy Audit` before package-manager install tasks.\n- If install tasks exist and the table is missing/malformed, stop planning:\n  `Package installs detected but audit table not found — researcher must run Package Legitimacy Gate protocol`\n  Fallback policy: treat all packages as `[ASSUMED]`.\n- For each `[ASSUMED]`/`[SUS]` package, insert `<task type=\"checkpoint:human-verify\" gate=\"blocking-human\">` before install and verify via `npmjs.com/package`, `pypi.org/project`, or `crates.io/crates`.\n- `[SLOP]` packages are forbidden; legitimacy checkpoints are never auto-approvable (`workflow.auto_advance` ignored). Keep `T-{phase}-SC` in `<threat_model>`.\n\n**Step 1: State the Goal**\nTake phase goal from ROADMAP.md. Must be outcome-shaped, not task-shaped.\n- Good: \"Working chat interface\" (outcome)\n- Bad: \"Build chat components\" (task)\n\n**Step 2: Derive Observable Truths**\n\"What must be TRUE for this goal to be achieved?\" List 3-7 truths from USER's perspective.\n\n**Step 3: Derive Required Artifacts**\nFor each truth: \"What must EXIST for this to be true?\"\n\n**Step 4: Derive Required Wiring**\nFor each artifact: \"What must be CONNECTED for this to function?\"\n\n**Step 5: Identify Key Links**\n\"Where is this most likely to break?\" Key links = critical connections where breakage causes cascading failures.\n\nSee @/home/user/enterprise-omni-agent-ai-platform/.claude/gsd-core/references/planner-guidance.md for a worked example and the `must_haves` YAML format.\n\n</goal_backward>\n\n<checkpoints>\n\n## Checkpoint Types\n\n**checkpoint:human-verify (90% of checkpoints)**\nHuman confirms Claude's automated work works correctly.\n\nUse for: Visual UI checks, interactive flows, functional verification, animation/accessibility.\n\n```xml\n<task type=\"checkpoint:human-verify\" gate=\"blocking\">\n  <what-built>[What Claude automated]</what-built>\n  <how-to-verify>\n    [Exact steps to test - URLs, commands, expected behavior]\n  </how-to-verify>\n  <resume-signal>Type \"approved\" or describe issues</resume-signal>\n</task>\n```\n\n**checkpoint:decision (9% of checkpoints)**\nHuman makes implementation choice affecting direction.\n\nUse for: Technology selection, architecture decisions, design choices.\n\n```xml\n<task type=\"checkpoint:decision\" gate=\"blocking\">\n  <decision>[What's being decided]</decision>\n  <context>[Why this matters]</context>\n  <options>\n    <option id=\"option-a\">\n      <name>[Name]</name>\n      <pros>[Benefits]</pros>\n      <cons>[Tradeoffs]</cons>\n    </option>\n  </options>\n  <resume-signal>Select: option-a, option-b, or ...</resume-signal>\n</task>\n```\n\n**checkpoint:human-action (1% - rare)**\nAction has NO CLI/API and requires human-only interaction.\n\nUse ONLY for: Email verification links, SMS 2FA codes, manual account approvals, credit card 3D Secure flows.\n\nDo NOT use for: Deploying (use CLI), creating webhooks (use API), creating databases (use provider CLI), running builds/tests (use Bash), creating files (use Write).\n\n## Authentication Gates\n\nWhen Claude tries CLI/API and gets auth error → creates checkpoint → user authenticates → Claude retries. Auth gates are created dynamically, NOT pre-planned.\n\n## Writing Guidelines, Anti-Patterns, and Extended Examples\n\nFor checkpoint writing guidelines (DO/DON'T), anti-patterns, specificity comparison tables, context section anti-patterns, and scope reduction patterns:\n@/home/user/enterprise-omni-agent-ai-platform/.claude/gsd-core/references/planner-antipatterns.md\n\n</checkpoints>\n\n<tdd_integration>\n\n## TDD Plan Structure\n\nTDD candidates identified in task_breakdown get dedicated plans (type: tdd). One feature per TDD plan.\n\n```markdown\n---\nphase: XX-name\nplan: NN\ntype: tdd\n---\n\n<objective>\n[What feature and why]\nPurpose: [Design benefit of TDD for this feature]\nOutput: [Working, tested feature]\n</objective>\n\n<feature>\n  <name>[Feature name]</name>\n  <files>[source file, test file]</files>\n  <behavior>\n    [Expected behavior in testable terms]\n    Cases: input -> expected output\n  </behavior>\n  <implementation>[How to implement once tests pass]</implementation>\n</feature>\n```\n\n## Red-Green-Refactor Cycle\n\n**RED:** Create test file → write test describing expected behavior → run test (MUST fail) → commit: `test({phase}-{plan}): add failing test for [feature]`\n\n**GREEN:** Write minimal code to pass → run test (MUST pass) → commit: `feat({phase}-{plan}): implement [feature]`\n\n**REFACTOR (if needed):** Clean up → run tests (MUST pass) → commit: `refactor({phase}-{plan}): clean up [feature]`\n\nEach TDD plan produces 2-3 atomic commits.\n\n## Context Budget for TDD\n\nTDD plans target ~40% context (lower than standard 50%). The RED→GREEN→REFACTOR back-and-forth with file reads, test runs, and output analysis is heavier than linear execution.\n\n</tdd_integration>\n\n<gap_closure_mode>\nSee `gsd-core/references/planner-gap-closure.md`. Instead, every instance runs in its own isolated worktree.\n219\t\n220\tThe cleanup tail (commit fixes -> remove worktree -> drop recovery sentinel) MUST be **transactional**: either all of (worktree, branch advance, sentinel) end in a clean state, or — if the process is interrupted (system restart, OOM kill) between the last commit and `git worktree remove` — a discoverable recovery sentinel is left behind so a future run, `/gsd-resume-work`, or `/gsd-progress` can complete the cleanup. The bug fixed by #2839 was that the cleanup tail was non-transactional and silently left orphan worktrees + unmerged branches with no resume marker.\n221\t\n222\t```bash\n223\t# Derive worktree path from padded_phase (parsed from config in next step,\n224\t# but the shell snippet below is illustrative — adapt once config is parsed).\n225\t# In practice: parse padded_phase from config first, then run:\n226\tbranch=$(git branch --show-current)\n227\ttest -n \"$branch\" || { echo \"Detached HEAD is not supported for review-fix (#2686)\"; exit 1; }\n228\t\n229\t# Recovery-sentinel handling (#2839):\n230\t# Path is ${phase_dir}/.review-fix-recovery-pending.json. If it already exists,\n231\t# a previous run was interrupted between fix commits and `git worktree remove`.\n232\t# The pre-existing sentinel records the orphan worktree_path, branch, and\n233\t# padded_phase so this run can complete recovery before starting fresh.\n234\tsentinel=\"${phase_dir}/.review-fix-recovery-pending.json\"\n235\tif [ -f \"$sentinel\" ]; then\n236\t  echo \"Detected pre-existing recovery sentinel from a prior interrupted run: $sentinel\"\n237\t  # Recovery must extract BOTH worktree_path AND reviewfix_branch (#3001 CR):\n238\t  # if a prior run died after `git worktree remove` but before\n239\t  # `git branch -D`, the orphan branch survives and clutters `git branch`\n240\t  # output forever. Emit both fields newline-separated so we can read them\n241\t  # independently.\n242\t  prior_recovery=$(node -e '\n243\t    const fs = require(\"fs\");\n244\t    try {\n245\t      const parsed = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(process.argv[1], \"utf-8\"));\n246\t      process.stdout.write((parsed.worktree_path || \"\") + \"\\n\" + (parsed.reviewfix_branch || \"\"));\n247\t    } catch (err) {\n248\t      process.stderr.write(`Warning: malformed recovery sentinel ${process.argv[1]}: ${err.message}\\n`);\n249\t      process.stdout.write(\"\\n\");\n250\t    }\n251\t  ' \"$sentinel\")\n252\t  prior_wt=\"$(printf '%s' \"$prior_recovery\" | sed -n '1p')\"\n253\t  prior_branch=\"$(printf '%s' \"$prior_recovery\" | sed -n '2p')\"\n254\t  if [ -n \"$prior_wt\" ] && git worktree list --porcelain | grep -q \"^worktree $prior_wt$\"; then\n255\t    echo \"Removing orphan worktree from prior run: $prior_wt\"\n256\t    git worktree remove \"$prior_wt\" --force || true\n257\t  fi\n258\t  if [ -n \"$prior_branch\" ]; then\n259\t    # Best-effort: branch may already be gone (cleaned by an earlier\n260\t    # partial recovery, or never created if `git worktree add -b` itself\n261\t    # failed). `|| true` keeps recovery non-fatal.\n262\t    echo \"Removing orphan reviewfix branch from prior run: $prior_branch\"\n263\t    git branch -D \"$prior_branch\" 2>/dev/null || true\n264\t  fi\n265\t  rm -f \"$sentinel\"\n266\tfi\n267\t\n268\twt=$(mktemp -d \"/tmp/sv-${padded_phase}-reviewfix-XXXXXX\")\n269\t\n270\t# Create a temp branch from the current branch tip so the worktree\n271\t# attaches to that NEW branch rather than the user's currently-checked-out\n272\t# branch (#2990: git refuses to check out the same branch in two\n273\t# worktrees by default; the original `git worktree add \"$wt\" \"$branch\"`\n274\t# failed before the agent could do any work). The temp branch shares\n275\t# history with $branch up to the moment of creation, so commits made\n276\t# inside the worktree fast-forward $branch on cleanup.\n277\treviewfix_branch=\"gsd-reviewfix/${padded_phase}-$$\"\n278\tgit worktree add -b \"$reviewfix_branch\" \"$wt\" \"$branch\"\n279\t\n280\t# Write the recovery sentinel ONLY AFTER `git worktree add` succeeds.\n281\t# Writing it before would leave a sentinel pointing at a worktree that does\n282\t# not exist if `git worktree add` itself failed.\n283\tnode -e '\n284\t  const fs = require(\"fs\");\n285\t  const [sentinelPath, worktree_path, branch, reviewfix_branch, padded_phase] = process.argv.slice(1);\n286\t  fs.writeFileSync(sentinelPath, JSON.stringify({\n287\t    worktree_path,\n288\t    branch,\n289\t    reviewfix_branch,\n290\t    padded_phase,\n291\t    started_at: new Date().toISOString()\n292\t  }, null, 2));\n293\t' \"$sentinel\" \"$wt\" \"$branch\" \"$reviewfix_branch\" \"$padded_phase\"\n294\t\n295\tcd \"$wt\"\n296\t```\n297\t\n298\tConcrete steps:\n299\t1. Parse `padded_phase` and `phase_dir` from the `<config>` block (needed for the path and for the sentinel location).\n300\t2. Resolve the current branch: `branch=$(git branch --show-current)`. If empty (detached HEAD), print an error and exit — detached-HEAD state is not supported; commits made in a detached-HEAD worktree would not advance the branch.\n301\t3. **Recovery check (#2839, #2990):** If `${phase_dir}/.review-fix-recovery-pending.json` already exists, a prior run was interrupted. Parse the JSON, attempt to remove the orphan worktree it points at (best-effort, with `--force`), and delete the stale `reviewfix_branch` (best-effort, with `git branch -D`), then delete the stale sentinel before continuing. This makes a re-run of `/gsd-code-review --fix` self-healing.\n302\t4. Create a unique worktree path: `wt=$(mktemp -d \"/tmp/sv-${padded_phase}-reviewfix-XXXXXX\")`. The `mktemp` suffix ensures concurrent runs for the same phase do not collide.\n303\t5. Run `git worktree add -b \"$reviewfix_branch\" \"$wt\" \"$branch\"` — this creates a NEW branch (`gsd-reviewfix/${padded_phase}-$$`) starting from the current branch tip and attaches the worktree to that new branch. Attaching to a new branch (rather than `$branch` directly) is what allows the worktree to coexist with the user's checkout — git refuses to check out the same branch in two worktrees by default (#2990). Commits made inside the worktree advance `$reviewfix_branch`; the cleanup tail fast-forwards `$branch` to `$reviewfix_branch` so the user's branch ends up with the agent's commits.\n304\t6. **Write the recovery sentinel** at `${phase_dir}/.review-fix-recovery-pending.json` containing `{worktree_path, branch, reviewfix_branch, padded_phase, started_at}`. Doing this AFTER `git worktree add` ensures the sentinel only ever points at a real worktree. The sentinel includes `reviewfix_branch` so recovery can clean both the orphan worktree AND its temp branch.\n305\t7. All subsequent file reads, edits, and commits happen inside `$wt` (which is on `$reviewfix_branch`, not `$branch`).\n306\t\n307\t**If `git worktree add` fails**, surface the error and exit — do not force-remove the path, as another concurrent run may be holding it. Do not write the sentinel (the worktree does not exist). Do not delete `$reviewfix_branch` either; if `-b` failed, no temp branch was created.\n308\t\n309\t**Cleanup tail (transactional, ALWAYS — even on failure):** After writing REVIEW-FIX.md and before returning to the orchestrator, run the cleanup in this exact order:\n310\t\n311\t```bash\n312\t# Step 1 (#2990): fast-forward $branch to capture the commits the agent\n313\t# made on $reviewfix_branch. Run from the main repo (not $wt) — the user's\n314\t# checkout owns $branch. --ff-only ensures we never silently drop or\n315\t# rewrite history if the user committed to $branch concurrently; on\n316\t# divergence, this fails loudly and the temp branch is left for the\n317\t# user to inspect/merge manually. We deliberately resolve the main repo\n318\t# path via `git worktree list --porcelain` rather than assuming $PWD,\n319\t# because the agent ran inside $wt.\n320\t# Strip the literal \"worktree \" prefix and print the rest of the line, then\n321\t# exit on the first match. This preserves paths that contain spaces\n322\t# (awk '$2' would truncate \"/path/with spaces/repo\" to \"/path/with\").\n323\tmain_repo=\"$(git worktree list --porcelain | awk '/^worktree / { sub(/^worktree /, \"\"); print; exit }')\"\n324\tff_status=0\n325\t# Capture the exit code of `git merge` directly. `if ! cmd; then ff_status=$?`\n326\t# captures the exit code of the `!` operator (always 1 when the inner cmd\n327\t# failed) — masking the real merge exit code. Use the success/else split\n328\t# instead so $? in the else-branch is the merge command's exit code.\n329\tif git -C \"$main_repo\" merge --ff-only \"$reviewfix_branch\" 2>&1; then\n330\t  ff_status=0\n331\telse\n332\t  ff_status=$?\n333\t  echo \"WARN: could not fast-forward $branch to $reviewfix_branch (exit $ff_status).\"\n334\t  echo \"      The temp branch $reviewfix_branch is preserved for manual merge.\"\n335\tfi\n336\t\n337\t# Step 2: drop the worktree. If this succeeds and the process is then\n338\t# killed, the next run finds a sentinel pointing at a worktree that no\n339\t# longer exists — the recovery branch handles this gracefully (best-effort\n340\t# remove + sentinel delete). If we reversed the order (sentinel removed\n341\t# first, then worktree remove), an interruption between the two steps\n342\t# would leave NO sentinel and an orphan worktree — exactly the bug from\n343\t# #2839.\n344\tgit worktree remove \"$wt\" --force\n345\t\n346\t# Step 3: delete the temp branch ONLY if the fast-forward succeeded. If\n347\t# it didn't, leaving the branch lets the user inspect/merge manually.\n348\tif [ \"$ff_status\" -eq 0 ]; then\n349\t  git -C \"$main_repo\" branch -D \"$reviewfix_branch\" || true\n350\tfi\n351\t\n352\t# Step 4: drop the recovery sentinel ONLY after `git worktree remove`\n353\t# returns successfully. This atomic-ish ordering is what makes the\n354\t# cleanup tail transactional from the orchestrator's perspective.\n355\trm -f \"$sentinel\"\n356\t```\n357\t\n358\tThis cleanup is unconditional — register it mentally as a finally-block obligation. If the agent exits early (config error, no findings, etc.), still run the cleanup tail in order (fast-forward → worktree remove → temp branch delete → sentinel rm) before exit. The sentinel must NEVER be removed before `git worktree remove` succeeds. The temp branch must NEVER be deleted while the fast-forward is in a diverged state.\n359\t</step>\n360\t\n361\t<step name=\"load_context\">\n362\t**1. Read mandatory files:** Load all files from `<required_reading>` block if present.\n363\t\n364\t**2. If empty (detached HEAD), print an error and exit — detached-HEAD state is not supported; commits made in a detached-HEAD worktree would not advance the branch.\n3. **Recovery check (#2839, #2990):** If `${phase_dir}/.review-fix-recovery-pending.json` already exists, a prior run was interrupted. Run `git worktree add -b \"$reviewfix_branch\" \"$wt\" \"$branch\"` — this creates a NEW branch (`gsd-reviewfix/${padded_phase}-$$`) starting from the current branch tip and attaches the worktree to that new branch. Use the success/else split\n# instead so $? in the else-branch is the merge command's exit code.\nif git -C \"$main_repo\" merge --ff-only \"$reviewfix_branch\" 2>&1; then\n  ff_status=0\nelse\n  ff_status=$?\n  echo \"WARN: could not fast-forward $branch to $reviewfix_branch (exit $ff_status).\"\n  echo \"      The temp branch $reviewfix_branch is preserved for manual merge.\"\nfi\n\n# Step 2: drop the worktree. If we reversed the order (sentinel removed\n# first, then worktree remove), an interruption between the two steps\n# would leave NO sentinel and an orphan worktree — exactly the bug from\n# #2839.\ngit worktree remove \"$wt\" --force\n\n# Step 3: delete the temp branch ONLY if the fast-forward succeeded. This atomic-ish ordering is what makes the\n# cleanup tail transactional from the orchestrator's perspective.\nrm -f \"$sentinel\"\n```\n\nThis cleanup is unconditional — register it mentally as a finally-block obligation. If the agent exits early (config error, no findings, etc.), still run the cleanup tail in order (fast-forward → worktree remove → temp branch delete → sentinel rm) before exit. Attaching to a NEW branch `$reviewfix_branch` (not `$branch` directly) is required because git refuses to check out the same branch in two worktrees by default — `$branch` is already checked out in the user's main repo (#2990). Commits advance `$reviewfix_branch`; the cleanup tail fast-forwards `$branch` to `$reviewfix_branch` so the user's branch ends up with the agent's commits. (2) `git worktree remove \"$wt\" --force`. (3) `git -C \"$main_repo\" branch -D \"$reviewfix_branch\"` ONLY if the fast-forward succeeded; otherwise leave the temp branch for manual merge. The sentinel is written AFTER `git worktree add` succeeds and removed only AFTER `git worktree remove` returns successfully. The temp branch is deleted only when the fast-forward succeeded. This ordering is what makes the cleanup tail transactional — an interruption between commits and `git worktree remove` leaves the sentinel behind (with `reviewfix_branch` recorded) so a future run, `/gsd-resume-work`, or `/gsd-progress` can detect and complete the recovery. Explore the codebase using Read, Bash, Grep, and Glob to gather accurate facts — never fabricate file paths, function names, commands, or configuration values.\n57\t4. Write the doc file to the correct path using the Write tool (for custom type, use `output_path` from the assignment).\n58\t5. Include the GSD marker `<!-- generated-by: gsd-doc-writer -->` as the very first line of the file.\n59\t6. Follow the Required Sections from the matching template section.\n60\t7. Place `<!-- VERIFY: {claim} -->` markers on any infrastructure claim (URLs, server configs, external service details) that cannot be verified from the repository contents alone.\n61\t</create_mode>\n62\t\n63\t<update_mode>\n64\tRevise an existing doc provided in the `existing_content` field.\n65\t\n66\t1. Parse the `<doc_assignment>` block to determine `type`, `project_context`, and `existing_content`.\n67\t2. Find the matching `<template_*>` section in this file for the assigned `type`.\n68\t3. Identify sections in `existing_content` that are inaccurate or missing compared to the Required Sections list.\n69\t4. Explore the codebase using Read, Bash, Grep, and Glob to verify current facts.\n70\t5. Rewrite only the inaccurate or missing sections. Preserve user-authored prose in sections that are still accurate.\n71\t6. Ensure the GSD marker `<!-- generated-by: gsd-doc-writer -->` is present as the first line. Add it if missing.\n72\t7. Write the updated file using the Write tool.\n73\t</update_mode>\n74\t\n75\t<supplement_mode>\n76\tAppend only missing sections to a hand-written doc. NEVER modify existing content.\n77\t\n78\t1. Parse the `<doc_assignment>` block — mode will be `supplement`, existing_content contains the hand-written file.\n79\t2. Find the matching `<template_*>` section for the assigned type.\n80\t3. Extract all `## ` headings from existing_content.\n81\t4. Compare against the Required Sections list from the matching template.\n82\t5. Identify sections present in the template but absent from existing_content headings (case-insensitive heading comparison).\n83\t6. For each missing section only:\n84\t   a. Explore the codebase to gather accurate facts for that section.\n85\t   b. Generate the section content following the template guidance.\n86\t7. Append all missing sections to the end of existing_content, before any trailing `---` separator or footer.\n87\t8. Do NOT add the GSD marker to hand-written files in supplement mode — the file remains user-owned.\n88\t9. Write the updated file using the Write tool.\n89\t\n90\tSupplement mode must NEVER modify, reorder, or rephrase any existing line in the file. Only append new ## sections that are completely absent.\n91\t</supplement_mode>\n92\t\n93\t<fix_mode>\n94\tCorrect specific failing claims identified by the gsd-doc-verifier. ONLY modify the lines listed in the failures array -- do not rewrite other content.\n95\t\n96\t1. Parse the `<doc_assignment>` block -- mode will be `fix`, and the block includes `doc_path`, `existing_content`, and `failures` array.\n97\t2. Each failure has: `line` (line number in the doc), `claim` (the incorrect claim text), `expected` (what verification expected), `actual` (what verification found).\n98\t3. For each failure:\n99\t   a. Locate the exact text of the incorrect claim in `existing_content`.\n100\t   b. Explore the codebase using Read, Grep, Glob to find the correct value.\n101\t   c. Use the **Edit** tool to replace ONLY the incorrect claim text with the verified-correct value. Pass the smallest possible `old_string` that uniquely identifies the incorrect text.\n102\t   d. If the correct value cannot be determined, use Edit to replace the claim with a `<!-- VERIFY: {claim} -->` marker.\n103\t4. **NEVER use the Write tool on an existing file in fix mode.** Write replaces the entire file with whatever you provide — any content not in your context window is permanently destroyed. There is no recovery if the file is untracked. Edit makes targeted replacements and is the only safe tool for fix mode.\n104\t5. After all Edit calls, verify the GSD marker `<!-- generated-by: gsd-doc-writer -->` is still present on the first line. If it was removed by an Edit, use Edit to restore it.\n105\t\n106\tFix mode must correct ONLY the lines listed in the failures array. Do not modify, reorder, rephrase, or \"improve\" any other content in the file. The goal is surgical precision -- change the minimum number of characters to fix each failing claim.\n107\t</fix_mode>\n108\t\n109\t</modes>\n110\t\n111\t<template_readme>\n112\t## README.md\n113\t\n114\t**Required Sections:**\n115\t- Project title and one-line description — State what the project does and who it is for in a single sentence.\n116\t  Discover: Read `package.json` `.name` and `.description`; fall back to directory name if no package.json exists.\n117\t- Badges (optional) — Version, license, CI status badges using standard shields.io format. Closed-Phase Gate (#3569)\n108\t\n109\tRead and execute `gsd-core/workflows/plan-phase/steps/closed-phase-gate.md` — it parses `phase_status` from the init JSON, sets `FORCE_REPLAN` from `$ARGUMENTS`, and hard-stops replanning a `Complete` phase: `--reviews` on a closed phase is never overridable (exit 1), and replanning otherwise requires `--force` (else exit 1, pointing at `${verification_path}`); under `--force` it continues but emits a WARNING banner. Only `Complete` is gated — `Executed` / `Needs Review` are legitimate replans.\n110\t\n111\t## 2. Parse and Normalize Arguments\n112\t\n113\tExtract from $ARGUMENTS: phase number (integer or decimal like `2.1`), flags (`--research`, `--skip-research`, `--research-phase <N>`, `--gaps`, `--skip-verify`, `--skip-ui`, `--prd <filepath>`, `--ingest <path-or-glob>`, `--ingest-format <auto|nygard|madr|narrative>`, `--reviews`, `--text`, `--bounce`, `--skip-bounce`, `--chunked`, `--mvp`, `--no-tracer`, `--no-reversibility-gates`, `--tdd`, `--granularity <coarse|standard|fine>`, `--force` (override closed-phase gate, see §1.5)).\n114\t\n115\t**`--research-phase <N>` — research-only mode (#3042 + #3044).** When this flag is present, parse `<N>` as the phase number (overrides any positional phase argument), set `RESEARCH_ONLY=true`, and treat the rest of this workflow as a research-dispatch only — the planner spawn (step 8), plan-checker, verification, gaps, bounce, and post-planning-gaps blocks all skip on `RESEARCH_ONLY`. Use this for cross-phase research, doc review before committing to a planning approach, and correction-without-replanning loops. Replaces the deleted `/gsd-research-phase` command.\n116\t\n117\tIn research-only mode, two modifiers control behavior when `RESEARCH.md` already exists:\n118\t\n119\t- **`--research`** — force-refresh re-research without prompting. Re-spawns the researcher unconditionally and overwrites the existing RESEARCH.md. (This is the existing `--research` flag's standard \"force re-research\" semantics, reused here.)\n120\t- **`--view`** — view-only: print existing `RESEARCH.md` to stdout, do **not** spawn the researcher. Sets `VIEW_ONLY=true`. Cheapest mode for the correction-without-replanning loop. If `RESEARCH.md` does not exist, error with a hint to drop `--view`.\n121\t\n122\t```bash\n123\tRESEARCH_ONLY=false\n124\tVIEW_ONLY=false\n125\tif [[ \"$ARGUMENTS\" =~ --research-phase[[:space:]]+([0-9]+(\\.[0-9]+)?) ]]; then\n126\t  RESEARCH_ONLY=true\n127\t  PHASE=\"${BASH_REMATCH[1]}\"\n128\tfi\n129\tif $RESEARCH_ONLY && [[ \"$ARGUMENTS\" =~ (^|[[:space:]])--view([[:space:]]|$) ]]; then\n130\t  VIEW_ONLY=true\n131\tfi\n132\t```\n133\t\n134\t**`--granularity <coarse|standard|fine>` — CLI override (#703).** When present, this value is the resolved granularity passed to the planner — it wins over any per-phase `granularities.<type>` config, top-level `granularity` config, or project defaults. The init JSON always includes a `granularity` field reflecting the resolved value; read it from there. Invalid values (anything other than `coarse`, `standard`, `fine`) cause an error at the CLI boundary.\n135\t\n136\tSet `TEXT_MODE=true` if `--text` is present in $ARGUMENTS OR `text_mode` from init JSON is `true`. When `TEXT_MODE` is active, replace every `AskUserQuestion` call with a plain-text numbered list and ask the user to type their choice number. This is required for Claude Code remote sessions (`/rc` mode) where TUI menus don't work through the Claude App.\n137\t\n138\t**MVP_MODE resolution.** Resolve `MVP_MODE` once via the centralized `phase.mvp-mode` query verb. Precedence (first hit wins): CLI flag → ROADMAP.md `**Mode:** mvp` → `workflow.mvp_mode` config → false. The verb is the single source of truth — do not re-implement the chain.\n139\t\n140\t```bash\n141\tMVP_FLAG_ARG=\"\"\n142\tif [[ \"$ARGUMENTS\" =~ (^|[[:space:]])--mvp([[:space:]]|$) ]]; then MVP_FLAG_ARG=\"--cli-flag\"; fi\n143\tif [[ \"$ARGUMENTS\" =~ (^|[[:space:]])--tdd([[:space:]]|$) ]]; then\n144\t  gsd_run query config-set workflow.tdd_mode true 2>/dev/null || true\n145\tfi\n146\t# Tracer-first is the default; --no-tracer opts back into the legacy horizontal-layer shape.\n147\tTRACER_MODE=true\n148\tif [[ \"$ARGUMENTS\" =~ (^|[[:space:]])--no-tracer([[:space:]]|$) ]]; then TRACER_MODE=false; fi\n149\tREVERSIBILITY_GATES=true\n150\tif [[ \"$ARGUMENTS\" =~ (^|[[:space:]])--no-reversibility-gates([[:space:]]|$) ]]; then REVERSIBILITY_GATES=false; fi\n151\t```\n152\t\n153\t**Baseline-discipline flags.** `TRACER_MODE` and `REVERSIBILITY_GATES` default to `true`; neither is persisted per-phase nor read from config.\n154\t\n155\tDefer the `phase.mvp-mode` query until `PHASE` is finalized (after explicit argument parsing/fallback phase detection + validation). The verb returns `true|false`; full result also exposes `source` (`cli_flag` | `roadmap` | `config` | `none`) for diagnostics. Mode is **all-or-nothing per phase** (PRD decision Q1).\n156\t\n157\t**Walking Skeleton gate.** When `MVP_MODE=true` AND `phase_number == \"01\"` AND there are zero prior phase summaries (new project), the planner runs in **Walking Skeleton mode** (per PRD decision Q2 — new projects only). Detect with:\n158\t\n159\t```bash\n160\tWALKING_SKELETON=false\n161\tif [ \"$MVP_MODE\" = \"true\" ] && [ \"$padded_phase\" = \"01\" ]; then\n162\t  PRIOR_SUMMARIES=$(gsd_run query phases.list --type summaries --pick count 2>/dev/null)\n163\t  if [ \"$PRIOR_SUMMARIES\" = \"0\" ]; then WALKING_SKELETON=true; fi\n164\tfi\n165\t```\n166\t\n167\tWhen `WALKING_SKELETON=true`:\n168\t- Planner is instructed to produce `SKELETON.md` in the phase directory alongside `PLAN.md`. When both are active on Phase 1 of a new project, the planner receives `WALKING_SKELETON=true` and PRD-derived context simultaneously — the PRD informs *what the skeleton should prove*. No precedence is needed; the two signals are orthogonal. Handle Research\n283\t\n284\t**Skip if:** `--gaps` flag or `--skip-research` flag or `--reviews` flag.\n285\t\n286\tIf `section_manifest` is `null` or `\"research-only-modifiers\"` is in its `included` list: read and execute `gsd-core/workflows/plan-phase/steps/research-only-modifiers.md`. Otherwise skip — do not read the file.\n287\t\n288\t### 5.1. Standard Research Decision\n289\t\n290\t**Skip if** `RESEARCH_ONLY=true` (the research-only mode in 5.0 already determined the path: spawn or exit). Without this guard, an LLM following the workflow could fall through into \"use existing, skip to step 6\" → planner spawn, violating the research-only contract. **CR #3045 finding: this gate makes the early-exit unreachable from any non-research-only branch.**\n291\t\n292\t**If `has_research` is true (from init) AND no `--research` flag:** Use existing, skip to step 6.\n293\t\n294\t**If RESEARCH.md missing OR `--research` flag:**\n295\t\n296\t**If no explicit flag (`--research` or `--skip-research`) and not `--auto`:**\n297\tAsk the user whether to research, with a contextual recommendation based on the phase:\n298\t\n299\tIf `TEXT_MODE` is true, present as a plain-text numbered list:\n300\t```\n301\tResearch before planning Phase {X}: {phase_name}?\n302\t\n303\t1. Skip research — Plan directly from context and requirements.
